extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing news stories about public meetings, legislative sessions, conventions, and investigations/hearings — how to select, arrange, and present material so it is accurate, significant, and engaging. Emphasizes treatment of testimony and the special quasi-judicial character of inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings stories include sessions of state legislatures, municipal councils, conventions of organizations, local society meetings, and investigations/hearings conducted by legislative committees; investigations and hearings are often more like judicial proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this classification to decide approach and conventions; recognize when a meeting story should follow ordinary meeting-report conventions versus quasi-judicial (court-like) treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — accuracy and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: To give the facts accurately and as completely as their significance warrants should be the first aim in reporting proceedings of official bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize factual correctness and appropriate completeness; avoid distortion or suppression of facts even when pursuing a constructive end (e.g., exposing sinister influences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid partisan misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The desire to accomplish some end does not justify distortion or suppression of the news of the doings of official bodies; politically partisan stories that misrepresent public matters are illegitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not misrepresent proceedings to create favorable opinion for the paper's cause — such practices harm the paper's reputation and public trust in newspapers generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show significance to readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear the significance of acts of representative public bodies in relation to the home and business interests of individual readers and to the welfare of the community, state, and nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect proceedings to readers' everyday concerns to foster intelligent interest in government; explain why the actions matter beyond raw procedural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment — make dry proceedings interesting
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief problem is to make interesting what is often considered dry and unattractive in proceedings of public meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple, clear explanation of meaning; lively accounts of debate; and vivid description of persons and scenes to increase interest. Seek legitimate humorous or pathetic phases to heighten interest when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of humorous or pathetic phases legitimately
rubrics_metrics.description: Some meetings contain humorous or pathetic phases that may be brought out legitimately to heighten interest and emphasize significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such elements only when genuinely part of the proceedings and when they illuminate significance; when overall news interest is slight these elements can produce acceptable human-interest stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the vital matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the parts of the proceedings that are of general interest and significance — these make up the contents of meeting stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating every incidental detail as important; focus on matters with public relevance and discard trivialities that distract from the core issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present concisely and condense routine details
rubrics_metrics.description: To present vital matters concisely and to condense routine but necessary details into the smallest possible compass requires effort and skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for brevity: compress background and routine procedure while preserving clarity; use paraphrase and summary to handle procedural minutiae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle testimony like court stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony in investigations and hearings sometimes has dramatic phases like that in court trials; the questions and answers in these proceedings are handled like those in court stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Q&A with attention to sequence, dramatic moments, and the import of testimony; treat witnesses' statements as you would in trial reporting — select salient exchanges and summarize lines of questioning that illuminate the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid playing up insignificant incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Insignificant incidents of casual interest are often played up as features of important meetings to the subordination or exclusion of matters of vital concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist temptation to foreground amusing or salacious side incidents when they eclipse substantive developments; ensure features do not displace core news.
